subbench.objective: An INSTRUMENT sentinel, not a survey: a small, FIXED set of short-call cells whose per-call time (tens of ns) is sensitive to the bench's OWN timing code, measured in EVERY window beside pcre2-jit as the flat control. [B133] (after [B132]): adding stamp getters to testees/pcrec/driver.c moved short calls +10-17% on program-identical cells, which looked like a pcrec regression for three weeks (O-92). If the sentinel shifts while pcre2-jit stays flat, the INSTRUMENT moved; if a pcrec cross-pin Delta on these cells is not echoed by the sentinel's own shift, it is the engine's.

testee.build_flags: rustc 1.98.1 (48a229cea 2026-09-01); `regex` crate 1.13.1 (crates.io, pinned by the COMMITTED testees/rust/Cargo.lock, inbox I-76); driver built with `cargo build --release`; regex::bytes::RegexBuilder (byte-haystack mode -- satisfies non-utf8-subject at the SUBJECT level; the PATTERN must still be valid UTF-8, a different, structural constraint -- see testees/rust/CLAUDE.md's I-72 section)
testee.compile_cost_definition: eager-jit-adjacent (capability_set_v1.md 7.1/7.2): the explicit RegexBuilder::build() call, timed in-driver (`compile`). CAVEAT: like re2-default/re2-longest, this call does NOT build the runtime DFA -- the `regex` crate's lazy DFA is built INCREMENTALLY at match time and cached (N2 5). A reader pooling this testee beside pcre2-jit under one eager-jit table is comparing two different compile-cost SHAPES that happen to share a class token; the reporter's 7.2 footnote fires on exactly this definition-string mismatch. Median of N with spread is the REPORTER's reduction.

named_count.description: distinct named capture groups in the pattern (testees/onig/adapter.py's `names` pair, same shape)

ncapturegroups.description: lexical capturing groups in the pattern (the overall match, group 0, is not counted -- the same convention testees/re2/adapter.py and testees/onig/adapter.py already use)

refusal_class.description: 'size-limit' for CompiledTooBig (size_limit or dfa_size_limit exceeded); 'syntax' for every other named variant, incl. the structural 'invalid UTF-8 pattern' refusal this adapter raises itself before the regex crate ever sees the pattern (see the I-72 section, testees/rust/CLAUDE.md)
refusal_class.source: the regex::Error variant name RegexBuilder::build() returned on a did-not-compile outcome, bucketed by this adapter (capability_set_v1.md 5.5: 'declared ONLY by a config whose engine gives a closed, structural signal' -- regex::Error's two named variants, Syntax and CompiledTooBig, are exactly that, and the type is #[non_exhaustive] so a third variant added upstream degrades to `syntax` rather than a crash)
